turns.user: Where can I find counseling services?
turns.agent:
Counseling services are available through several confidential, free resources offered across the Marine Corps and Department of Defense. Depending on your needs, you can connect with installation-based programs or access support worldwide.

Key counseling resources include:

* **MCCS Community Counseling Program (CCP):** Provides free, confidential, short-term non-medical counseling for active-duty service members and their eligible dependents. Clinicians assist with everyday challenges such as relationship issues, stress management, grief, communication, and work-life balance. Records are maintained separately from military medical records.
* **Military & Family Life Counselors (MFLC):** Licensed professionals embedded directly within units, installations, and youth programs. They offer free, confidential, short-term non-medical counseling on or off the installation, and no records are kept.
* **Military OneSource:** Offers up to 12 free sessions of non-medical counseling per issue via telephone, secure video, online chat, or in-person with a local provider. Available 24/7 worldwide by calling **800-342-9647** or visiting [MilitaryOneSource.mil](https://www.militaryonesource.mil).
* **Installation Chaplains:** Offer 100% confidential counseling and spiritual guidance for personal, relational, and moral issues, with complete confidentiality.
* **Immediate Crisis Support:** If you or someone you know is experiencing an urgent mental health crisis, contact the **Military Crisis Line** 24/7 by dialing **988 (Press 1)**, texting **838255**, or chatting online.

### Next Steps

Because specific office locations, direct phone lines, and appointment walk-in hours vary by installation, please let me know your base (e.g., Camp Pendleton, Camp Lejeune, MCB Quantico, MCB Camp Butler / Okinawa, or MCAS Miramar), and I will provide the local contact information and facility details.

Sources
* [Military OneSource - Non-Medical Counseling](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/confidential-help/non-medical-counseling/military-and-family-life-counseling/)

turns.user: How do I sign up for childcare at Quantico?
turns.agent:
To sign up for childcare at Marine Corps Base Quantico, you must submit a request for care online through **MilitaryChildCare.com**, which manages placement and waitlists for all Department of Defense child care programs.

### How the Process Works

* **Submit a Request Online:** Create an account on **MilitaryChildCare.com**, complete your household profile, search for care options at MCB Quantico, and submit requests for your desired programs.
* **Available Programs at Quantico:**
  * **Child Development Centers (CDC):** Full-day care for infants and children ages 6 weeks through 5 years (prior to kindergarten).
    * **CDC North:** Bldg. 3311 Purvis Road | (703) 784-4470
    * **CDC South:** Bldg. 3314 Purvis Road | (703) 784-3652
    * *CDC Operating Hours:* Monday – Friday, 6:00 AM – 6:00 PM
  * **Family Child Care (FCC):** Certified home-based care for ages 6 weeks to 12 years.
  * **School Age Care (SAC):** Before/after school and camp care for school-age youth at Bldg. 3312 Purvis Road | (703) 784-2249.
* **Receive an Offer:** When a space becomes available based on DoD priority guidelines, you will receive an offer through MilitaryChildCare.com. You must accept the offer within the stated window.
* **Finalize Registration:** After accepting an offer, the Quantico Resource & Referral office will provide enrollment paperwork. You will need to provide:
  * Updated child immunization records
  * Current Leave and Earnings Statements (LES) or proof of income/school status for both parents to determine fees (based on DoD Total Family Income tiers)
  * Completed health assessment and emergency contact forms

### Next Steps

1. Visit **MilitaryChildCare.com** to create your profile and place your child on the Quantico waitlist as early as possible.
2. Contact the **Quantico CYP Resource & Referral Program** at **(703) 784-0674** or **(703) 784-4453** (Bldg. 3311 Purvis Road; Mon–Fri 7:30 AM – 4:30 PM) for assistance with placement questions or enrollment status.

### Sources

* [MilitaryINSTALLATIONS - MCB Quantico Child and Youth Programs](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/resources/installations/quantico/?view=programs-services&service=child-and-youth-programs)

turns.user: What kind of programs does the fitness center offer at Camp Pendleton?
turns.agent:
MCCS Camp Pendleton’s Semper Fit program operates 13 fitness centers across the installation—including the flagship Paige Fieldhouse (Bldg 1110)—offering a broad range of strength conditioning, tactical readiness, and wellness programs for service members, families, retirees, and DoD civilians.

Key programs include:

* **Group Fitness (Group X):** Aerobic and strength classes offered at locations like Paige Fieldhouse and 21 Area Fitness Center. Classes include indoor cycling, yoga, STRONG Nation, LES MILLS Virtual programs (RPM Cycle, Body Balance), family fitness, and fee-based options like Zumba and youth dance. Most standard classes are free for authorized patrons.
* **High Intensity Tactical Training (HITT):** Combat-focused strength and conditioning designed for active-duty personnel. Programs focus on speed, power, mobility, injury prevention, and readiness, with certified coaches, dedicated HITT areas/lockers, and instructor courses (Level 1 and 2).
* **Human Performance Assessments:** Degreed professionals provide specialized fitness testing, including resting metabolic rate (RMR), VO2 Max, and body fat/body composition testing (BCP support). Assessments are available at Paige Fieldhouse and several area gyms (including 14, 21, 22, 31, 43, 53, and 62 Area facilities).
* **Health & Wellness Education:** Classroom instruction and workshops covering Nutrition 101, BCP Nutrition & Fitness, injury prevention, sleep hygiene, chronic disease prevention, and free tobacco cessation courses.
* **Unit Physical Training (PT):** Units can schedule dedicated PT sessions led by Semper Fit instructors, including specialized combat conditioning, functional fitness, and unit yoga.
* **24/7 Gym Access:** Eligible CAC cardholders can register for free 24/7 unstaffed access at select facilities, including Paige Fieldhouse and the 21 Area Fitness Center.

### Next Steps
1. **Schedule an Assessment or Class:** Call the Paige Fieldhouse Human Performance Office at (760) 763-3793 for metabolic testing and nutrition consultations, or the Fitness Programs Office at (760) 763-0657.
2. **Register for 24/7 Access:** Visit the front desk at a participating facility (such as Paige Fieldhouse, Bldg 1110) during staffed hours to complete the registration waiver.
3. **Unit PT Inquiries:** Reach out to the fitness department supervisor at (760) 763-0657 to reserve instructor-led training for your unit.

***

### Sources
* [MCCS Camp Pendleton Paige Fieldhouse & Group X](https://usmc-mccs.org)
* [MCCS Camp Pendleton Human Performance](https://usmc-mccs.org)

turns.user: When does youth soccer registration open at MCAS Miramar?
turns.agent:
Youth soccer registration at MCAS Miramar opens seasonally rather than on a single fixed date. Registration for **Spring Soccer** generally opens in late winter (typically mid-to-late December or January), while registration for **Fall Soccer** generally opens in late summer (around July or August).

**Key Registration Details:**
* **Seasonal Cycles:** MCAS Miramar Youth Sports typically runs two soccer seasons each year—Spring Soccer (playing March through May) and Fall Soccer (playing October through December), as well as Start Smart Soccer programs for ages 3–5.
* **Registration Availability:** Slots are filled on a first-come, first-served basis. Once a division reaches capacity, participants are placed on a waitlist (no fee is charged for waitlisted athletes).
* **Required Documentation:** All participants must have an up-to-date Youth Sports Health Assessment form on file. If the athlete has an indicated diagnosis, a current Sports Inclusion Assessment Team (IAT) form is also required prior to participation.
* **Eligibility:** Open to dependents (ages 3–17) of active-duty military, reservists, retirees, and DoD civilian employees.

**Contact & Office Information:**
* **Location:** MCAS Miramar Youth & Teen Center / Youth Sports Office (Bldg. 2700, Moore Ave)
* **Phone:** (858) 307-6530
* **Email:** OMBMiramarYouthSports@usmc-mccs.org
* **Youth Sports Office Hours:** Monday–Thursday: 11:00 AM – 7:30 PM; Friday: 1:00 PM – 9:30 PM; Saturday–Sunday: Closed

### Next Steps
1. **Contact the Youth Sports Office:** Call (858) 307-6530 or email OMBMiramarYouthSports@usmc-mccs.org to confirm the upcoming registration release date and verify team age divisions.
2. **Prepare Medical Forms:** Ensure your child's annual Health Assessment form is completed and signed before registration opens to prevent delays.
3. **Register Promptly:** Complete registration online or at the Youth Center as soon as the portal opens to secure a roster spot before divisions fill.

***

### Sources
* [MilitaryINSTALLATIONS – MCAS Miramar Youth Services](https://www.militaryonesource.mil/resources/installations/mcas-miramar/)
* [MCCS Miramar Child and Youth Programs](https://miramar.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth)
